what_it_does: DNA-CIM uses resistive RAM (RRAM, a type of non-volatile memory that can also perform computations) to accelerate DNA sequence matching and mutation detection. By performing comparisons directly in the memory array instead of shuttling data between separate memory and processing units, the design reduces energy consumption and improves throughput for genomic analysis. DNA sequences are converted to binary for bitwise operations, with specialized sensing circuits to detect mismatches.
